public_rationale: The original preview documentation explicitly said Recall did not perform content moderation and would not hide passwords or financial account numbers. That supports the ordinary reading that it lacked automatic protection based on content sensitivity. Manual exclusions and other privacy controls do not contradict this narrower claim. The conclusion applies to the announcement-era preview.
limitations: The primary wording survives here in a contemporary secondary source.
This does not mean Recall lacked all privacy controls.
Later versions are outside the target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft's AI-powered Recall feature cannot distinguish ordinary computer usage from sensitive information such as passwords or health data.

statement.excerpt: Despite being an inherently AI-powered feature, it can’t distinguish between ordinary computer usage and genuinely sensitive information — like passwords, health information, or trade secrets that must be protected at all costs.

from_speaker: passwords, health information, or trade secrets
our_interpretation: It refers to the original Recall preview announced shortly before the post.
The ordinary reading is that Recall did not automatically recognize sensitive screen content and exclude or redact it because of its sensitivity.
User-selected app or website exclusions, private-browsing exclusions, and password masking performed by another application do not establish automatic sensitive-content recognition.
The target period is the announcement-era preview from May 20 through June 3, 2024. Later implementations are outside scope.
criteria.support_condition: Publication-era documentation or testing establishes that Recall captured visible sensitive information without automatic content-sensitive filtering or redaction.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documentation or reproducible tests establish that the original preview automatically recognized and protected sensitive content of the kinds described.
